subject: DI03000081

body.en:
Understand the idea

Acurrent-carrying conductor in a magnetic field experiences force;the commutator maintains useful unidirectional torque.

Explanation and application

  • Lorentz force:F=q(E+v×B);for the relevant conductor,F=BIl sinθ.The force direction follows conventional current,not electron flow.
  • Fleming left hand:index field, middle current,thumb force/motion.All three are perpendicular.Reverse either armature current or field flux to reverse torque;not both together.
  • Rotation induces Eb=PΦZN/(60A)opposing the applied supply by Lenz law.In the stated steady-state model V=Eb+IaRa+Vbrush,and Ia=(V−Eb−Vbrush)/Ra.
  • At start,N=0so Eb=0and Raissmall;unlimited starting current can damage the armature/starter.Aload increase reduces speed/Ebtemporarily,raising Iato develop more torque.
  • Back EMFis a conversion indicator:developed mechanical power=EbIa.Never "remove back EMF"as a supposed efficiency improvement.
Why a starter?

Eb=0at standstill and Rasmall,so starting current needs limitation.

Understand the idea

Distinguish developed armature torque from useful shaft torque.

Explanation and application

  • Converted power Pdev=EbIa;angular speed ω=2πN/60.Ta=Pdev/ω=PZΦIa/(2πA)newton-metres.
  • Thus Ta=0.15915(PZ/A)ΦIaapproximately.Rotational losses use part of developed power,so Tsh=Ta−Trotat nonzero speed.
  • Shaft output=2πNTsh/60watts;Tsh=9550Pout(kW)/Napproximately.Keep rpm and rad/s distinct.
  • Brake horsepower is shaft output expressed in mechanical horsepower:BHP=Pout/745.7Wapproximately.It is not input power and is not the same unit as metric horsepower.
  • Ta∝ΦIa;the formula at N=0is obtained from the machine constant,not by dividing zero developed power by zero speed.

h.gu: Motor Converted Power તથા Shaft Output

body.en:

title.gu: 2.3 Motor Types તથા ત્રણ Characteristic Curves

h.en: Motor types and three characteristic curves
h.gu: Motor Types તથા ત્રણ Characteristic Curves

body.en:
Understand the idea

Classify by excitation first,then relate speed and torque to current.

Explanation and application

  • Shunt:field across supply,approximately constant Φ;Ta∝Ia.Speed N∝(V−IaRa)/Φfalls slightly as current rises;its N–Tacurve is a slightly drooping near-constant-speed curve.
  • Series:field carries Ia;below saturation Φ∝Iaand Ta∝Ia².After saturation Taapproaches proportionality to Ia.Speed falls strongly with load/current.
  • Aseries motor must never be run without its approved mechanical load;low current weakens flux and can produce dangerous overspeed.Coupling/load-loss risk needs protection.
  • Cumulative compound combines shunt base flux with assisting series flux:high starting torque with better speed restraint than a series motor.Differential compound can be unstable and is rarely suitable for general drives.
  • Separately excited and permanent-magnet motors suit controlled drives within their thermal/current limits.The same general torque/speed equations apply with the correct flux model.
  • Plot N–Ia,Ta–Iaand N–Taseparately;do not label shaft torque as developed torque unless losses are accounted for.

Understand the idea

The plotted shapes are ideal qualitative trends,not measured manufacturer curves.

Explanation and application

  • For shunt flux held fixed,increasing Iaadds resistive voltage drop and lowers speed slightly.Compensating controllers can change the observed characteristic.
  • For series operation the low-load extrapolation is not an allowable test region;keep the declared operating load and speed limit.

Understand the idea

Use the same current/flux model to connect the first two characteristic curves.

Explanation and application

  • Shunt flux approximately constant:torque rises with Iaand speed droops slightly.Series flux grows with current before saturation,giving strong speed reduction with increasing torque.
  • Cumulative compound lies between characteristic tendencies according to its field strengths;the plot is conceptual,not a universal manufacturer curve.Series no-load region is omitted for safety.

Understand the idea

N∝(V−IaRtotal−Vbrush)/Φunder the stated steady-state magnetic conditions.

Explanation and application

  • Shunt armature-voltage control lowers speed below base speed at approximately constant field;an approved controlled DCdrive is preferable to wasting power in resistance.
  • Armature resistance control inserts series resistance,lowering armature voltage under load.Speed depends strongly on load and I²Rloss makes it inefficient.
  • Shunt flux control increases field resistance to reduce If/Φand raise speed above base speed only within limits.Never open a running shunt field.
  • Series flux control uses approved field diverter/tapped-field arrangements;a diverter reduces field current for given armature current.Armature diverter affects current/torque differently.
  • Series armature/total-voltage and series-resistance methods need the actual series circuit model.Never assume Φconstant before saturation or compare different loads without justification.
  • Check current,commutation,speed,thermal and load-torque limits after every calculated control change.Field weakening reduces available torque per ampere.

Given and assumptions

V220V,Ra0.5Ω,Ia20A,N1=1000rpm,brush drop neglected;same armature current for the declared comparison.

Step-by-step solution

  1. Eb1=210V.At unchanged flux,target N2=800rpmrequires Eb2=168V.Rtotal=(220−168)/20=2.6Ω;add2.1Ω.
  2. Added-resistor dissipation=20²×2.1=840W.It is a rating/efficiency warning,not an instruction to improvise a resistor.
  3. At same voltage/current but Φ2=0.8Φ1,speed would be1250rpm,while torque becomes0.8of its former value.Check the permissible speed/load.

Interpretation and check

Same Iaand reduced flux do NOTrepresent the same torque load;constant-torque comparisons need a revised current.

title.gu: 2.5 Starter શા માટે અને તેની Protection

h.en: Why a starter and how its protections work
h.gu: Starter શા માટે અને તેની Protection

body.en:
Understand the idea

At standstill Eb=0;the starter limits current until rising back EMFallows resistance to be removed.

Explanation and application

  • Two-point starter:series motor line/armature path includes starting sections and release mechanism;current through the series circuit provides holding action in the approved design.
  • Three-point:L(line),A(armature),F(field).Starting resistance is in the armature circuit;no-volt coil(NVC)is in series with the shunt field and overload release(OLR)responds to armature current.
  • With loss of supply or field-circuit interruption,the three-point holding coil releases the spring-return handle.Aweak field used for speed control can also cause nuisance release.
  • OLRopens the holding circuit on excessive current;it is not a substitute for correct fusing,isolation,earthing,field-loss or overspeed protection.
  • Follow approved handle/step timing and return-to-OFFrules;never tie the handle in RUN,bypass releases or advance a stalled machine.

Understand the idea

Four-point operation is included because practical10explicitly asks it,even though the main theory line lists two/three-point starters.

Explanation and application

  • Two-point series starter must be matched to a loaded series machine and its current-release design;it does not make no-load running safe.
  • Four-point adds a separate supply return for its holding coil;NVCis across the supply through its own limiting resistance,independent of shunt-field current.
  • Therefore intentional field weakening does not release the four-point NVC,but field failure alone may not release it either.Separate field-loss/overspeed protection is essential as appropriate.

Understand the idea

Aguarded brake applies mechanical load while speed,input and effective force are measured.

Explanation and application

  • Identify drum effective radius,load-measurement units,rated speed/current and approved cooling/guarding before any test.Friction heats the brake rapidly.
  • If force readings are newtons,T=(F1−F2)r;if masses are kilograms,T=(m1−m2)gr.Use effective radius including rope contribution when relevant.
  • Pout=2πNT/60;η=Pout/total electrical input.Include separately supplied field power if applicable;shunt field already lies in line input.
  • Series brake tests retain safe mechanical load throughout starting/running/stopping and stop on load-loss indications.Do not remove the brake load while energised.

Understand the idea

Run an appropriate shunt machine at rated no-load voltage/speed and estimate losses;this is not a load-capacity demonstration.

Explanation and application

  • At no load Ia0=IL0−If.Estimated rotational+iron loss=VIL0−VIf−Ia0²Ra−brush loss0.
  • For predicting shunt-motor efficiency at chosen line current,use Ia=IL−If;add field,copper,brush and estimated fixed losses to obtain total losses.
  • For predicting shunt-generator efficiency at chosen load current,use Ia=IL+Ifand η=VIL/(VIL+losses).Do not use the motor-current subtraction for a generator.
  • Limitations:load-dependent stray losses,temperature-dependent resistance,commutation and full-load heating are not directly demonstrated;assumed constant flux/speed must be stated.Not suitable for unloaded series motors.

Given and assumptions

V220V,IL0=3A,If1A,Ra0.5Ω,brush loss neglected;predict at20Aline/load using the stated approximate constant-loss model.

Step-by-step solution

  1. Ia0=2A;rotational/iron loss=660−220−2=438W.Field loss220W.
  2. Motor:line20A,armature19A;loss=438+220+19²×0.5=838.5W;Pout3561.5W;η80.9432%.
  3. Generator:load20A,armature21A;loss878.5W;input5278.5W;η83.3570%.

Interpretation and check

Predictions depend on the stated loss model,not fabricated loaded observations.

Understand the idea

Choose torque-speed behaviour and maintenance requirements before selecting a DCmotor.

Explanation and application

  • Shunt:near-constant-speed machine tools,fans and suitable conveyors;good speed regulation but limited starting torque relative to a comparable series design.
  • Series:high starting torque for appropriate traction/hoist duties with engineered load/overspeed protection;unloaded running is forbidden.
  • Cumulative compound:presses,elevators or drives needing starting torque plus speed restraint,subject to actual duty rating.
  • Advantages:controllable speed,strong starting torque for selected types and straightforward torque-current relationships.Limitations:brush/commutator maintenance,sparking,losses and restricted hazardous-area suitability without certified design.
